rationale: Use a broad mid-temperature scouting gradient to elute all 10 compounds if possible and map the overall elution window without biasing selectivity too far. The wide phi range and moderate slope reduce the risk of truncated runs while giving informative spacing patterns for later refinement.

All peaks eluted well within the gradient, with the first around phi_e ~0.11 and the last around phi_e ~0.59, so trim the gradient window to concentrate resolving power where the compounds actually elute. Keeping tG and T fixed isolates the effect of a narrower phi range, which should spread the crowded mid-cluster and improve CRF by reducing unnecessary gradient range and run time.

The broad window was clearly better, so now test slope directly by halving tG while holding phi and T constant. This will show whether the critical mid-cluster is slope-sensitive and may improve CRF if the run can be shortened without pushing the worst pair below acceptable resolution.

The crowded mid-cluster is strongly slope-sensitive: shortening to 10 min caused the 5–7 region to collapse, while 20 min resolved it well but paid a time penalty. Test an intermediate slope to recover enough resolution on the critical pair while keeping the run short enough to beat the 20 min method on CRF.

The optimum appears to lie between 14 and 20 min, with the 6/7 pair improving markedly as the gradient is made shallower. Try 16 min at the same phi window and temperature to see if a small gain in the critical resolution can reach the CRF maximum while preserving the zero time penalty.

At 14 min the only deficiency is the nearly inseparable 6/7 pair, which looks only modestly slope-responsive near the optimum, so temperature is the next lever for selectivity. A 5 C decrease may alter that close pair enough to improve the resolution term while keeping the run short and likely still at zero time penalty.

Lowering temperature worsened selectivity, indicating the critical cluster is temperature-sensitive; now test the opposite direction. A 5 C increase at the current near-optimal slope may improve the 6/7 separation enough to beat the 40 C result while likely keeping the run within the zero-penalty region.

Temperature changes in either direction worsened the critical cluster, so keep 40 C and refine slope instead. Since 16 min restored baseline resolution with only a small time penalty and 14 min gave the best CRF so far, 18 min tests whether a slightly shallower gradient can reach full resolution while preserving a competitive overall score.

The active elution window only extends to about phi_e ~0.56 for the last peak, so phi1 = 0.95 is likely wasting gradient range and steepening the effective program through the crowded middle. Reducing phi1 to 0.85 at the proven 14 min, 40 C conditions tests whether a narrower high-end window can selectively spread the mid-cluster without sacrificing full elution.

The reduction from phi1 0.95 to 0.85 improved CRF and still gave full elution, suggesting excess high-organic range was unnecessary. Step phi1 down once more to 0.80 to see whether the crowded mid-cluster gains a bit more spacing while keeping the run short enough to preserve or improve the score.

The optimum in phi1 appears bracketed: 0.80 increases run time too much, while 0.85 is the current best and 0.95 is slightly worse on resolution. Test 0.90 to see if it trims just enough time relative to 0.85 while maintaining full resolution, potentially nudging CRF closer to 1.0.

Injection 11 is very close to optimal but still limited by the 6/7 pair, so keep the improved phi window and make the gradient slightly shallower. If 0.90 retains the zero time penalty at 16 min, the gain in the critical resolution could push the CRF to the maximum.

With phi1 = 0.90, making the gradient shallower caused too much time penalty, so the optimum likely sits near 14 min on the fast side. Test 12 min to map the other side of that optimum and confirm whether 14 min is truly best or whether a slightly steeper run can keep the score high enough despite some loss in the 6/7 separation.

The first peak is still comfortably retained, so raising phi0 slightly may trim unneeded low-organic range and concentrate more of the gradient across the central cluster. This tests whether a modest upward shift of the window improves the critical 6/7 spacing or shortens the run enough to surpass the current best.

Injection 14 is extremely close to ideal, so probe locally around that optimum by slightly expanding the upper end of the window while keeping the beneficial higher phi0. This may reduce the mild compression around the critical 6/7 pair or slightly shorten late retention enough to find the true maximum.

The local optimum is clearly near phi0 = 0.10, so test the symmetric move on the upper end by lowering phi1 from 0.90 to 0.85. This checks whether the current best can be improved by slightly narrowing the working window around the actual elution region while preserving the favorable selectivity pattern.

We have already reached the maximum CRF, so use remaining runs only to probe whether the optimum is broad or uniquely centered. Raising phi0 one more step while keeping the winning phi1, tG, and T tests whether further trimming the low-organic portion preserves the perfect score or starts to erode the critical early/mid selectivity.

Two neighboring methods now give CRF 1.000, so continue mapping robustness by raising phi0 another step at otherwise identical conditions. This tests how far the low end can be increased before the earliest compounds become too compressed or effectively unretained.

The perfect region appears to span phi0 = 0.10–0.15 at phi1 = 0.85, so now test whether a slightly lower phi1 remains on the plateau when combined with the better low-end trimming. This helps define the boundaries of the optimum around the current maximum without changing slope or temperature.

The plateau includes phi0 = 0.10–0.15 with phi1 = 0.85, and phi1 = 0.90 was nearly optimal at lower phi0, so test the remaining adjacent corner of this local design space. This will define whether the maximum extends toward slightly higher phi1 when paired with the stronger low-end trimming.

The only untested adjacent corner around the perfect plateau is phi0 = 0.15, phi1 = 0.80. Running it will complete the local map and confirm whether the optimum region is centered specifically at phi1 = 0.85 or extends lower when paired with the higher phi0.

The maximum has already been reached, so use the remaining budget to test robustness under deliberately different selectivity conditions around the winning window. A steeper gradient at higher temperature should reveal whether the critical pair remains the only liability and whether any alternate selectivity regime exists, while avoiding repetition of earlier methods.

The perfect region is defined at tG = 14 min, and steeper programs generally collapse the 6/7 pair, but the higher phi0 methods were especially robust. Test the best higher-phi0 window at 12 min to determine whether the plateau extends to a faster gradient under the most favorable windowing conditions.

With the optimum already achieved, use one of the last runs to measure temperature robustness of the winning window itself. The lower-temperature analogue of the best method has not been tested, and it will show directly how much of the perfect score depends on holding 40 C versus the phi window alone.

For the final run, test the lower-temperature robustness of the other CRF 1.000 method to complete the comparison between the two optimal windows. This directly shows whether phi0 = 0.15 is any less temperature-sensitive than phi0 = 0.10 while staying adjacent to the proven optimum.
